title: Preparing Bryophyte Specimens for DNA Extractions for Sanger Sequencing
author: Laura L Forrest
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bbieikbe
materials: We add roughly a microcentrifuge tube lid sized piece of plant tissue to the microcentrifuge tube for DNA extraction. We select the appropriate microcentrifuge tube (1.5 ml or 2 ml) based on the homogenization method that we are going to use. For most material we use a 2 ml tube and a QIAGEN TissueLyser. For higher-throughput processing, we put the dried plant material and beads into 1.2 ml QIAGEN collection microtubes and grind these in plates of 96 samples.
Proceed to chosen DNA extraction method.

steps.title: Prepare Herbarium Specimens
steps.instruction: Process herbarium material using a dissecting microscope to select samples and exclude fragments of other bryophytes.

substeps.instruction: Avoid material that has been rewetted for morphological examination.
If the plant must be dampened for identification or substrate removal, proceed with extraction immediately to avoid further DNA loss from re-drying.
Place any unused rehydrated and dried material into a separate, labeled subpacket before returning it to the herbarium packet.

steps.title: Prepare Silica-Gel Dried Specimens
steps.instruction: Clean and dry fresh field-collected bryophytes using a dissecting microscope.

substeps.instruction: Remove minute fragments of other plants, grit, soil, and insects using forceps and water.
For complex thalloid liverworts, strip scales and rhizoids from the thallus underside using a razor blade or forceps to remove organic matter and PCR inhibitors.
Place the physically cleaned bryophyte immediately into silica gel to dry.
Store long-term in ziplock bags with silica gel (preferably in the dark) or remove dry tissue and place in low-humidity cabinets.
Optional: House fragile collections in small tight-sealing petri dishes (e.g., Gelman sterile Petri Dishes 50x11) within low humidity cabinets.

steps.title: Annotate DNA Vouchers
steps.instruction: Identify and label the DNA voucher (either the sampled herbarium specimen or the specimen from the same collection as the silica-gel dried tissue).

substeps.instruction: Annotate the packet to indicate it is the DNA voucher.
Deposit vouchers in publicly accessible herbaria.

steps.title: Homogenize Fresh Bryophyte Material
steps.instruction: Grind fresh tissue in a 1.5 ml microcentrifuge tube using a disposable plastic pestle.

substeps.instruction: Add a pinch of acid-washed sand and a small amount of extraction buffer (buffer choice depends on the subsequent extraction protocol).
Optional: Use liquid nitrogen to freeze the tube and sample; if used, do not add buffer until immediately after grinding.

steps.title: Homogenize Dry Bryophyte Material
steps.instruction: Disrupt herbarium or silica-gel dried material using a Retsch™ Mixer Mill, QIAGEN TissueLyser, or equivalent.

substeps.instruction: For 2 ml microcentrifuge tubes: Use 1-2 3 mm conical tungsten beads; grind at 20 Hz for 4 minutes, stopping and rotating samples after the first 2 minutes.
For 1.2 ml QIAGEN collection microtubes: Use 1.5-2 mm ball bearings; grind at 20 Hz for 4 minutes.
